chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Al-Husayn ibn Thuwayr ibn Abi Fakhitah, from Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام), who said:
The Imamate does not return to be among two brothers after Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn, ever.
Rather, it proceeded from Ali ibn Al-Husayn,
just as Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: “And those of kinship are nearer to one another in the Book of Allah.”
So after Ali ibn Al-Husayn (عليه السلام), it is not to be except in the descendants and the descendants of the descendants.

key_terms.أَخَوَيْنِ: two brothers, indicating a fraternal succession
key_terms.أُولُوا الْأَرْحَامِ: those bound by kinship or blood relations
key_terms.الْإِمَامَةُ: the divinely appointed leadership of the Imams

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain that the Imamate continues through the descendants of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This hadith states that after Imam al-Hasan and Imam al-Husayn (عليهما السلام), the Imamate does not pass between two brothers again. It explains that the line of Imamate continues from Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (عليه السلام) through direct descendants, and supports this with the Quranic principle of nearer blood relations.
